newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end lower as gold falls.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end lower as gold falls.

text.p: The Australian share market closed lower on Tuesday as sentiment softened slightly and the gold sector dived over three percent in response to the falling price of bullion.
The All Ordinaries index lost 9.1 points to 2,400.7.
Brokers said there were few positive signals to compensate for the dip in the gold price and domestic economic data that showed a flat economy.
"It's a bit softer with the Dow shaky and gold off," said a Sydney dealer, adding that local signals remained far from positive.
"Local data is not showing great strength and that has created uncertainty on the domestic front."
November building approvals fell 1.6 percent and while retail sales rose 0.7 percent in the same period, economists said the result was hardly indicative of a strong economy.
"In anyone's language, the retail sector was weak in late 1996," said Stephen Koukoulas, chief economist at Citibank Australia.
Gold stocks continued their downward run with the gold index dipping 3.3 percent over the day. So far in 1997 the industry index has lost 6.7 percent.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about nine to five, while about 28 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
